title: A Promise for the Garden Revisited
premise: Lena Vane has spent ten years answering anonymous letters left in the lighthouse garden's stone wall, falling in love with a voice she never met. When the letters stop, she assumes the stranger moved on—until Elias Marsh, the vineyard's new consulting agronomist, moves in next door and she recognizes his handwriting. Their slow, wary courtship collides with her discovery that the vineyard's owner is quietly evicting the coastal families who tend it, and that Elias was hired to help. Choosing justice over safety, Lena and Elias expose the scheme before the first harvest, and in the aftermath they finally risk whole hearts instead of borrowed pieces.
about_author: Dominic Reyes is a former maritime archivist who writes love stories set where the land meets stubborn water. He lives on the northern coast with his partner and an untidy herb garden he refuses to weed.

chapters.title: The Wall That Keeps Secrets
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Tending her late grandfather's lighthouse garden, Lena finds the stone-wall letter slot empty for the first time in a decade. She rereads old letters, admitting how much of her inner life belongs to an unseen stranger. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Good Timing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. New to the coast as the vineyard's agronomist, Elias rents the cottage next door and recognizes Lena at the harbor without letting on who he is. He carries guilt about why he really came. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by concealment.

chapters.title: What the Vine Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lena and Elias collide over a shared fence line and a dying grapevine; their banter turns electric. She notices something familiar in his penmanship but dismisses it. Emotional beat: reluctant attraction taking root.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashbacks reveal Elias wrote the letters after a childhood debt to Lena's grandfather, then stopped when shame over his employer's plans made him feel like a fraud. Emotional beat: guilt pressing against desire.

chapters.title: The Eviction Notices
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena learns the vineyard owner is pressuring longtime tending families to sign away their plots. She organizes neighbors in secret, using the garden wall as a message board—their own justice outside the law. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the night before first harvest, Elias nearly confesses everything; instead they share a kiss interrupted by an eviction notice nailed to the lighthouse door—with Elias's signature on the survey attached. Emotional beat: intimacy shattered by betrayal.

chapters.title: Ink and Accusation
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Confronting Elias, Lena matches his handwriting to the letters and feels a decade of trust collapse. She banishes him from the garden. Emotional beat: heartbreak weaponized into cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Loft
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias finds falsified yield ledgers proving the owner manufactured the eviction pretext, and must choose between career and conscience. He copies the evidence and leaves it in the wall for Lena. Emotional beat: redemption through sacrifice.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At dawn of harvest day, Lena presents the ledgers to the assembled families and the county recorder; the scheme collapses publicly, and the community claims its plots. Elias stands exposed and unflinching beside her. Emotional beat: vindication entwined with vulnerability.

chapters.title: A Promise, Revisited
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weeks later, Elias answers one final letter placed in the wall—in person, reading it aloud among the vines. Lena offers him not pieces of her heart but all of it, and he stays. Emotional beat: belonging earned, love made whole.
